channel.title: russh.work / Writing
channel.description: Thesis posts, ship notes and field notes by Russell Harris.

item.title: Inside Double Double Bot: buying edge instead of favorites in a Yes-only prop market
item.description: Double Double Bot estimates each NBA player's double-double probability from ten seasons of box scores and picks by edge against de-vigged two-way prices, not by likelihood, because FanDuel prices the favorites above their realized rates. It runs on free data and a laptop, on paper stakes, until 100 picks show positive fair closing line value.

item.title: Ship Note: Bid Desk v1, a public-contracts pipeline for a prime we have not formed yet
item.description: An agent sweeps SAM.gov and the DMV portals and grades every find, a hosted hub shows two partners the pipeline, and nothing gets bid until the company exists.

item.title: Field Note: what it took to make an AI demand map safe to sell
item.description: A demand heat map that worked in demo mode met funded API accounts and real clients. Five defects surfaced in two weeks, every one caught by a gate before shipping, and a sixth seven weeks later. Field notes on what broke, what the fixes cost, and why the guardrails were the product.

item.title: Field Note: a season of strikeout picks that hit 80 percent on the alt line
item.description: 492 pitcher strikeout picks over 109 game days, 383-95 at the posted alt line, every one regraded against Statcast. How a conservative-floor strategy ran unattended all season, where the money came from, and the one upgrade for 2027.

item.title: Inside DealCalc: a CRM built around a spreadsheet nobody wants to retire
item.description: A residential wholesale and flip operator runs his acquisitions on one Excel workbook and a Mac app he commissioned years ago. The brief was a CRM his team can work in, with the analyzer inside it, that does not change a single number he already trusts. These are the six decisions that carried it, including why the workbook's own mistakes are reproduced on purpose and how a richer financing model ships without touching the first one.

item.title: Inside Content Bot: the questions that became the architecture
item.description: A client came to me tired of arguing with ChatGPT: re-pasting her rules every morning, watching the model ignore them, regenerating, losing the thread, fixing the same violations by hand. We replaced that loop with a system that carries her rules permanently and enforces them mechanically. This post is about the part that made it work, which was not the pipeline. It was the discovery interview. The questions I asked, the answers that became hard-coded rules, and the Forward Deployed engineering decisions that followed. The client is real and every number is from production.

item.title: Field Note: five failures that returned success
item.description: In one evening across four systems, every defect that mattered exited clean. A download job that moved nothing, a classifier that dropped a third of its input at the buzzer, an email that addressed its recipient in the third person. Notes on the dominant failure mode of model-assisted building, the three defenses that catch it ranked by what they cost, and one wrong diagnosis of my own.

item.title: Field Note: what 1,000 inputs found in an extraction pipeline
item.description: One user report became a 2,000-compile evaluation across five channels. It surfaced two bugs in my own metrics before it surfaced any in the product, the worst defect never threw an error, and the fix that mattered was moving a rule out of the prompt into code that can fail.

item.title: Inside CookSpec: compiling any recipe into one merge table
item.description: A recipe notation from 2004 that solved the format problem and was ignored for twenty years, rebuilt as an extraction pipeline. Any TikTok, Reel, article or photo compiles into one merge table with every unit normalized and checked against a density table.

item.title: Inside my agentic workflow: spec, fan-out, verify
item.description: How I actually ship with agents. Two shapes, a sequential contract pipeline and a parallel fan-out, both gated by evals. The spec comes before the prompt, the merge happens in plain code, and nothing ships unless the gate is green.

item.title: Inside the fit judge: an LLM-as-judge that corrected my own labels
item.description: An LLM-as-judge scores how well a resume fits a role, gated by a regression suite over a human-labeled golden set. It disagreed with my labels twice and was right both times, caught overqualification that keyword matching cannot, and was non-deterministic at temperature zero until self-consistency voting fixed it. A field guide to building an eval you can actually trust.

item.title: Inside Adoption Chain: an auditable second-order research engine for small-cap equity
item.description: Turns a PM's scenario into a consequence map, finds the under-covered small-cap companies on each consequence, and drafts a one-page thesis per name where every claim links to the exact SEC filing sentence. Leverage underneath judgment, never a recommendation.

item.title: Inside StrikeOut Bot: quantile regression and beat-the-baseline discipline for MLB strikeout prediction
item.description: Three LightGBM quantile regressors produce a median and a 90 percent interval, a Ridge stacker blends them against a dumb baseline, and a stratified blind test on unseen post-All-Star-Break data is the only gate that lets a model ship.

item.title: Inside Study Quest: five architectural decisions in a mastery-gated learning app
item.description: A gamified, mastery-gated catch-up learning PWA built for my son. Ship for the platform you can deploy from, pick the model on cost, put the integrity boundary in the database, grade only what the model is good at, and make the reward economy a config.

item.title: Ship Note: I built a way to watch the watch party
item.description: The Knicks are up 2-0 in the Finals and the Game 3 watch party got scattered across three parks. So in one evening I built a way to watch the watch party, using New York's public traffic cameras as a stand-in live feed.

item.title: Field Note: turning NYC's public traffic cameras into a live feed
item.description: New York DOT puts roughly 957 traffic cameras online as still images with no key and no login. Refresh one on a timer and a still becomes a feed. How I found the right cameras for each location, faked live without the page jumping, and handled the cameras that quietly die.

item.title: Inside Atlas: a 19-signal composition scorer for off-market real estate
item.description: Atlas surfaces off-market real estate leads by composing 19 distinct signal types across 568,135 parcels in Wake and Durham counties, with vision signals scored by Gemma 3 27B and a total POC spend of $54.

item.title: Inside Marketing Bot v2: five architectural decisions in a multi-pass orchestration system
item.description: Five architectural decisions in a multi-pass orchestration system, the alternatives rejected, and what each teaches about FDAA judgment in high-quality-bar long-context generation. The implementation is mine. The reasoning is portable.

item.title: Inside MES Open: five architectural decisions in an algorithmic trading system
item.description: Five architectural decisions in an algorithmic trading system targeting the New York open on Micro E-mini S&P 500 futures. The alternatives rejected, and what each teaches about FDAA judgment in a high-noise low-sample domain.

item.title: Inside the corridor pipeline: Python automation for LIHTC research
item.description: A 15-script Python pipeline that fuses Census ACS, HUD QCT, IRS OZ, USDA Food Atlas, state DDD, and land bank inventory data on a parcel key, scores against the state QAP, and produces an LP-memo-ready output.

item.title: Inside TrialEdge: a calibrated probability ensemble for FDA catalyst prediction
item.description: TrialEdge predicts FDA PDUFA catalyst outcomes. 4,032 tracked entities, 208 labeled outcomes, AUC 0.686 on the held-out set. The architecture is intentionally small, intentionally calibrated, and intentionally cheap.

item.title: Inside the Mosaic feasibility workflow: how I underwrite CRE deals with Claude
item.description: The Mosaic feasibility workflow is a Claude prompt suite that produces bank-quality CRE feasibility studies in 90 minutes instead of 30 hours.

item.title: Inside DeckTrainer: a Simply-Piano-style coaching tool for the Hercules DJControl
item.description: DeckTrainer is a learn-to-DJ coaching tool for the Hercules DJControl Starlight and Mix. Scope discipline, hardware-constraint surfacing, phased build plan.

item.title: Field Note: stacking R/ECAP, QCT, OZ, and DDD for LIHTC competitive advantage
item.description: Five public-records distress designations on a single parcel. The Mosaic framework to stack them, and the AI architecture that compresses three weeks of research to three hours.

item.title: Field Note: matching a $25M hospitality deal to five lenders in thirty minutes
item.description: Hospitality debt sourcing as constraint satisfaction followed by ranking. The architecture that compresses a week of broker research into thirty minutes.

item.title: Field Note: the NOI projection gap and why hospitality sponsors systematically over-promise
item.description: A coastal hospitality asset has an appraisal-stabilized NOI and a sponsor pro forma that differ by 17 percent. The gap decomposes into four components.

item.title: Field Note: reading a brokerage flyer through an AI underwriting lens
item.description: A brokerage marketing flyer is the highest-volume unstructured document in CRE. Four lines actually matter. The AI-architected workflow that closes the gap.

item.title: Field Note: packaging an emerging sponsor for institutional capital
item.description: An emerging sponsor faces a structural problem in the capital stack: senior debt is reachable, LP equity is the wall. The four packaging patterns institutional LPs evaluate against.

item.title: Field Note: the Obsidian-Claude Code loop for project tracking and roadmaps
item.description: Obsidian as the human-facing planning layer, Claude Code as the execution layer, both reading the same file system. Conventions, failure modes, what changes at team scale.

item.title: Field Note: Discord as the second screen for Claude Code activity
item.description: Discord webhooks for AI alerts: ship notifications, build failures, long-task completions, daily summaries. Hook architecture and channel layout.

item.title: Field Note: Perplexity deep research as the synthesis layer for binary and trinary decision trees
item.description: Map the decision as a tree of binary or trinary branches, write a per-node Perplexity prompt, let the model synthesize, then come back to the node and decide.
